title: Straight to the Milky Way's heart
caption: A laser guide star aimed at the Milky Way's centre, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A laser beam from Yepun, an 8.2-metre telescope of ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT), points straight at the centre of our galaxy, right into the heart of the Milky Way's brightest region. The galactic plane is crossed by prominent dark lanes, vast clouds of interstellar dust that block visible light.
The beam belongs to the VLT's adaptive optics system, making an artificial star 90 km up in Earth's mesosphere, which serves as a reference for correcting images and spectra for atmospheric blurring.

Although dust hides the galactic core from visible light, Yepun carries infrared instruments that can see through it. With them, astronomers study the complex, turbulent centre of the Milky Way, where a supermassive black hole lurks. The VLT consists of four 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes, of which Yepun is UT4, and four movable Auxiliary Telescopes of 1.8 metres.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based visible-light photograph by G. Hüdepohl; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Like this photograph, the eye cannot see through the dust lanes; only infrared instruments such as those on Yepun can peer into the galactic core.
